items.prompt: White to move. Black has just recaptured with the queen, which now stands on d5; each side has spent one move on a rook pawn (a3 and ...a6). Find the developing move that attacks the queen.

claims.statement: 3.Nc3 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
After 3.Nc3 one white piece, the knight, attacks the queen on d5.
After 2...Qxd5 the e-file is half-open for White (no white e-pawn) and the d-file is half-open for Black (no black d-pawn).

hints: Which white piece can come out and hit the queen?
The queen on d5 can be attacked by a knight from c3.
Name the square: it is on the queenside, beside the c-pawn.
items.explain: 3.Nc3 develops a piece and attacks the queen, so Black must spend a move on it. At depth 16 it is the engine's first choice.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen on a5 attacks the knight on c3, and the knight stands in front of the white king. White is ahead in development. Find one of the two moves the engine rates highest.

claims.statement: Bd2 and Nf3 are within 15 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).
One black piece, the queen on a5, attacks the knight on c3.
Be3 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Count the developed pieces for each side. Who is ahead?
The queen on a5, the knight on c3 and the king on e1 stand on one diagonal.
A bishop move or a knight move both fit.
items.explain: Bd2 and Nf3 are within 15 centipawns of each other and of the best move at depth 16: White keeps developing while Black's queen has moved twice. Be3 is at least 0.4 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.c1e3: Be3 develops, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.4 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move. The queen has moved twice and White has two knights out and the d-pawn in the centre. Find one of the two moves the engine rates highest.

claims.statement: Bf5 and c6 are within 15 centipawns of each other (depth 16).
The bishop on c8 has 5 legal moves: the d-pawn is gone, so its diagonal is open.
...Bg4 is at least 20 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which of Black's pieces is still at home and has room to move?
The bishop on c8 is not blocked by a pawn.
Either the bishop to f5 or a pawn to c6.
items.explain: The c8 bishop has five legal moves because the d-pawn left the file, so developing it is cheap here. At depth 16 ...Bf5 and ...c6 are within 15 centipawns of each other. The tempting ...Bg4 is at least 0.2 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.c8g4: ...Bg4 develops and attacks the knight on f3, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.2 pawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black to move; the queen is attacked by the knight on c3. A check is tempting. Find a queen move that gives up the least.

claims.statement: Qa5, Qd6 and Qd8 are within 10 centipawns of each other (depth 16).
One white piece, the knight on c3, attacks the queen on d5.
...Qe6+ is at least 15 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
...Qe5+ is at least 15 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The queen has to move, but where it goes matters.
Giving check with the queen is not automatically good. What can White answer with?
Three queen moves are close; the checks are not among them.
items.explain: Qa5, Qd6 and Qd8 are within 10 centipawns of each other at depth 16. The checks ...Qe6+ and ...Qe5+ are each at least 0.15 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.d5e6: ...Qe6+ is a check, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.15 pawns worse than the best queen moves.
feedback_by_move.d5e5: ...Qe5+ is a check, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.15 pawns worse than the best queen moves.

claims.statement: Nf3 and d4 are within 15 centipawns of each other and of the best move (depth 16).

hints: Who is ahead in development?
The queen has moved twice.
Open the centre or bring a piece out.
items.explain: Nf3 and d4 are within 15 centipawns of each other at depth 16. Other quiet moves may be fine too; the app marks these two.
